source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 4 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
A difference of two \(\sin^{-1}\) angles, answer in \(\sin^{-1}\).
Plan: find the two square roots and use formula (ii) directly.
steps:
Given: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{12}{13}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\).
To prove: their difference is \(\sin^{-1}\frac{33}{65}\).
Method: formula (ii) \(\sin^{-1}x - \sin^{-1}y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1-y^{2}} - y\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)\) with \(x = \frac{12}{13}\), \(y = \frac{3}{5}\). For positive \(x, y\) its condition \(xy \ge 0\) holds.

Find the square roots
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{144}{169}} = \tfrac{5}{13}\]
\[\sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{9}{25}} = \tfrac{4}{5}\]
Why: triples 5, 12, 13 and 3, 4, 5.

Apply formula (ii)
\[\text{L.H.S} = \sin^{-1}\left(\tfrac{12}{13}\cdot\tfrac{4}{5} - \tfrac{3}{5}\cdot\tfrac{5}{13}\right)\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\left(\tfrac{48}{65} - \tfrac{15}{65}\right)\]
\[= \sin^{-1}\tfrac{33}{65} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Why: each number is multiplied by the root of the other: \(x\) with \(\sqrt{1-y^{2}}\), \(y\) with \(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\). \(13 \times 5 = 65\).

Check
\[\sin^{-1}\tfrac{12}{13} - \sin^{-1}\tfrac{3}{5} \approx 1.1760 - 0.6435\]
\[= 0.5325\]
\[\sin^{-1}\tfrac{33}{65} \approx 0.5325\ \checkmark\]
Why: a calculator in radian mode agrees.
